title: Opencode voice
content:
1. Give OpenCode a Voice Layer

• Add a voice MCP plugin: Install a voice MCP integration such as jarvis-mcp (npx @shantur/jarvis-mcp --install-opencode-config --local and npx @shantur/jarvis-mcp --install-opencode-plugin --local) to stream voice messages into OpenCode sessions locally.
• Wire up speech-to-text and text-to-speech: Pair browser speech recognition/synthesis or real-time voice APIs (such as ElevenLabs, Deepgram, or LiveKit) with your assistant workflow so it listens and speaks back.

2. Define Persona, Rules, and Modular Skills

• Create specialized skills: Add modular instructions in .opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (project-level) or ~/.config/opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (global) so OpenCode loads domain capabilities on demand rather than cramming everything into one prompt.
• Set persona and guardrails: Write Markdown rules defining tone, permissions, and environment boundaries (for example, separating safe read/planning workflows from staging or execution agents).

3. Connect Tools, MCP Servers, and Local Models

• Add MCP servers and browser/web tools: Connect Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers for documentation or external services, and add automation tools like Playwright for browser control or web search tools.
• Run local-first models if desired: You can run opencode serve backed by a local engine like OpenJarvis through an OpenAI-compatible provider so OpenCode handles tool execution while local models supply inference.
• Plan before executing: Use OpenCode's agent/planning modes to review implementation plans before letting the agent modify files or run commands.
